population.span: randomized clinical trial among 360 consecutive candidates for cardiac surgery enrolled in 11 Italian centers between March 2012 and March 2014.

endpoint.span: main secondary study end points were postoperative AF and pericardial or pleural effusion.

estimate.span: postoperative AF (colchicine, 61 patients [33.9%]; placebo, 75 patients [41.7%]; absolute difference, 7.8%; 95% CI, -2.2% to 17.6%)

ci.span: postoperative AF (colchicine, 61 patients [33.9%]; placebo, 75 patients [41.7%]; absolute difference, 7.8%; 95% CI, -2.2% to 17.6%)

treatment_strategy.span: Patients were randomized to receive placebo (n=180) or colchicine (0.5 mg twice daily in patients ≥70 kg or 0.5 mg once daily in patients <70 kg; n=180) starting between 48 and 72 hours before surgery and continued for 1 month after surgery.

absent_reason: analysis_set: No source explicitly identifies the analysis population for the main postoperative AF estimate as ITT or all randomized. follow_up: The abstract does not specify the AF estimate's observation window; the registry specifies a protocol time frame of 3 months but does not explicitly link that window to the reported estimate.
served_mismatch: The served arm-level event counts agree with the abstract. However, the reported effect and CI are an absolute difference, not RR. The served ITT label and in-hospital/index-admission timepoint are not explicitly supported; the registry instead specifies a 3-month protocol window.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Registry eligibility specifies adults who are candidates for cardiac surgery, excluding transplantation.
entry_population_matches_question.span: Inclusion Criteria: * Age \> 18years * Candidate to cardiac surgery but cardiac transplantation * Informed consent

notes: Registry evidence is used for adult eligibility. Denominators are randomized arm sizes, not explicitly stated analysis denominators. The printed absolute difference is placebo minus colchicine; its CI must not be treated as an RR CI. No RR or RR CI was calculated.
